desc: G_m(u) = sn dn/cn = u + (1 - 2m) u^3/3 + 2(1 - m + m^2) u^5/15 + ...: the bend reads kappa = 1 - 2m
G'^2 = 1 + 2 kappa G^2 + G^4 with kappa = 1 - 2m: the law's logarithm is int dt / sqrt(1 + 2 kappa t^2 + t^4)
extra: max err 6.89e-41 over 5 points, incl. complex u and m

desc: our k = 0 laws are the perfect squares: (1 + d t^2)^2 = 1 + 2d t^2 + d^2 t^4 (kappa = d, quartic coeff = kappa^2)
Edwards addition (x^2 + y^2 = 1 + m x^2 y^2) read in the slope t = x/y is G(u) (+) G(v) = G(u + v)
G has two periods, 2K (real) and 2iK' (imaginary): a torus. One period only at m = 0 (pi, turning) and m = 1 (i pi, walls)
Wick rotation u -> iu swaps the two sides: G_m(iu) = i G_{1-m}(u), i.e. kappa -> -kappa
at m = 1/2 the torus is square: K = K'
slope chart: R(m) = 6/5 - 9/(10 kappa^2) with kappa = 1 - 2m
any odd chart with log' = 1/sqrt(1 + 2 kappa t^2 + eps t^4): R = 6/5 - (9/10) eps/kappa^2 (linear in the scale-free number eps/kappa^2)
ends: eps = kappa^2 (our conic laws, tan and tanh) gives 3/10; eps = 0 (arcsin, the sine chart) gives 6/5
x = sn chart: R = 6(1 - m + m^2)/(5(1 + m)^2), the same formula with kappa = -(1+m)/2, eps = m; symmetric under m -> 1/m
slope chart R is Wick-symmetric, R(m) = R(1 - m), a function of m(1 - m) only (as j is)
m = 1/2 (kappa = 0, square torus): G = u + u^5/10 + u^9/120 + ..., only powers u^(4j+1): the class jumps from contact 3 to contact 5
extra: iterative residue of the contact-5 class: 5/3 = 1.666667

desc: heights move the fingerprint: R(G^s) = R(G)/s for every real s (sympy, generic m and s)
normal form: G_0.2^(1/2) equals a rescaled elliptic generator at m' = 0.25666787 through u^5 exactly; they part at u^7
extra: u^7 gap -0.0080286, u^9 gap -0.0015924; a change of chart absorbs the rest formally, since (contact, R) is a complete formal invariant

desc: the Julia series (iterative logarithm) of G_m diverges at m = 0 and 0.2: heights live on petals, not as convergent series (as for e^x - 1)
a pendulum of amplitude theta0 has m = sin^2(theta0/2), so the curvature reading is kappa = 1 - 2m = cos(theta0)
integrating the pendulum: the slope reading t = omega sin(theta)/theta_dot is exactly G_m(omega time) (amplitudes 34, 90, 149 deg)
the wall: G has its pole at u = K, the turning point theta_dot = 0 (the pendulum turns back: turning country)
at the separatrix m -> 1 the half period K diverges like ln(4/sqrt(1-m)): relativity's wall is the top reached in infinite time
at m = 1 the slope chart is tanh and its law is velocity addition (our k = 0, d = -1)
half a height twice is one step: G^(1/2)(G^(1/2)(x)) = G(x) at m = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8
the half height of the m = 0.2 law against the rescaled m' law: close but not equal on [0, 0.8] (the u^7 gap)
heights add: G^s(G^(1-s)) = G for s = 1/2, -1/2, 3/2 at m = 0.8
Jacobi triple product: sum_n q^(n(n-1)/2) z^n = prod (1 - q^n)(1 + z q^(n-1))(1 + q^n/z)
prod_j (1 + z q^j) = 1 + (z o1 zq o1 zq^2 o1 ...): theta is the lift of the mult-add fold over the Tate orbit (both ways)
grouping the corners of that infinite cube by size gives Euler's sum z^n q^(n(n-1)/2)/(q;q)_n: corner weight q^(sum of positions)
theta's zeros sit at z = -q^(-j): mult-add's one wall at -1, copied once round each turn of the torus
as q -> 0 only the corners n = 0, 1 survive: tau -> 1 + e^(2kx), our lift, and u -> 2k^2 sech^2(kx), the KdV soliton
for q > 0 the same tau is a cnoidal wave: u solves the KdV travelling-wave equation u'' + 3u^2 - c u = A
